title: The Reader's Circle
kicker: A social home for people who read deeply
summary: A collaborative reading platform for discovering books, sharing reviews, and building a personal reading life with other readers.
description: The Reader's Circle brings book discovery, thoughtful discussion, and personal shelves into one welcoming reading space. Its Java and Spring backend powers a React and TypeScript frontend designed to make browsing, sharing, and keeping track of your reading feel effortless.
stack: Java, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud, MySQL, React, TypeScript

sections.title: The idea
sections.body: The platform gives readers a place to find their next book, share a point of view, and keep a record of what they have read. Discovery, discussion, and personal shelves work together instead of living in separate tools.

sections.title: The build
sections.body: The application uses Spring Boot and Spring Cloud, MySQL for persistence, and a React and TypeScript interface designed around quick browsing. The architecture keeps the reading experience simple while giving each part of the product a clear responsibility.

sections.title: The experience
sections.body: Readers can move from finding a title to exploring reviews and saving it to a personal shelf without losing context. The interface is organized for scanning, with focused book information and social details appearing exactly when they are useful.

title: Voice Cloning for ALS Patients
kicker: Preserving identity through personalized speech synthesis
summary: A speech-generation system designed to restore natural, personalized voice output for ALS patients using dysarthric speech adaptation and speaker-aware synthesis.
description: This machine learning project explores how personalized speech technology can support people whose natural voice is changing. The pipeline combines dysarthric speech data, speaker adaptation, and neural vocoding.
stack: Python, PyTorch, SpeechT5, LSTM, HiFi-GAN, FastAPI, TORGO

sections.title: The challenge
sections.body: Dysarthric speech can make communication difficult while still carrying the qualities that make a person's voice recognizable.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: The system combines speaker-aware adaptation with sequence modeling and neural vocoding. FastAPI exposes the inference workflow behind an application interface.

title: CommitGen LoRA: AI Git Hook
kicker: Conventional commits generated privately from staged code
summary: An AI Git hook that writes conventional commit messages from a staged diff using a locally hosted, LoRA fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 Coder model.
description: CommitGen LoRA reads the staged diff and recent commit history when you run git commit, then pre-fills the commit editor with a message such as fix(auth): handle expired token on refresh. The complete workflow runs offline, so source code never leaves your machine.
stack: Python, PyTorch, Unsloth, PEFT/LoRA, Qwen 2.5 Coder, GGUF, Ollama, Git hooks

sections.title: The workflow
sections.body: The Python hook collects the staged diff and recent commit history, sends a compact prompt to Qwen 2.5 Coder through Ollama, validates the generated conventional commit, and opens the editor with the result.

sections.title: The training
sections.body: I fine-tuned the model with QLoRA using Unsloth on a curated dataset of code diffs and commit messages, then exported the adapter to a compact 5.7MB GGUF artifact.

sections.title: The guardrails
sections.body: Diff truncation keeps prompts bounded, output validation prevents malformed messages, and a fallback to Git's default message keeps committing available when Ollama is not running.

title: Offside Detection Using Computer Vision
kicker: Perspective-aware football analysis from one broadcast image
summary: Detects offside players in football images using pitch-line vanishing points and jersey-color team assignment, built with OpenCV and geometry rather than a trained model.
description: This project decides whether attacking players are offside in a single football match image. Because broadcast cameras view the pitch at an angle, the pipeline corrects perspective before comparing player positions against the last defender.
stack: Python, OpenCV, NumPy, Hough transform, HSV color segmentation, perspective geometry
previewAlt: Abstract preview for football offside detection

sections.title: Team and goal direction
sections.body: Players are grouped into teams from pose annotations. The defending jersey color identifies the defending side, while the goalkeeper's position provides the goal direction.

sections.title: Vanishing-point geometry
sections.body: An adaptive HSV green mask isolates the pitch. Canny edges and a Hough transform find pitch markings, whose filtered pairwise intersections are averaged to estimate the vertical vanishing point.

sections.title: Projection and decision
sections.body: Each player's point closest to the goal line is projected along a line through the vanishing point. Those projections are compared with the last defender, then rendered with player outlines, the last-man line, offside lines, and labels.
